Because this generation claims to close that residual, and because closing it would end a standing disagreement between the two reviewers, I tested it in both directions: I looked for reasons the closure fails, and I also checked whether I was holding it to a standard no design contract could meet. shouldFix.appliesTo: PTCB-V33-B1 / PTCB-V33-S1 — the no-replacement policy is sound, but its mandatory present-state check inverts the security ordering and the requested capability binding was not added
shouldFix.title: kexecLoadDisabledNow refuses when /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled is absent, which is precisely the state of a kernel built without kexec support, so the configuration on which replacement is structurally impossible fails while a replacement-capable one passes
shouldFix.theFinding: kexecLoadDisabledNow reads 'read /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled. MUST be exactly 1 with optional newline. Absent file or any other value refuses', and both refusal enumerations list 'kexec_load_disabled not 1' as a refusal condition, so the check is mandatory. That sysctl is registered by the kexec core, so a kernel built without kexec support does not expose the file at all. Such a machine therefore refuses. It must also carry the required token sysctl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1 in its authenticated OptionalData under tokenRules, where it sets a sysctl that does not exist. The result is that a kernel on which no kexec path exists — the strongest possible state for the property being enforced — is refused, while a kernel that retains every kexec path and merely has the toggle set passes.
shouldFix.relationToTheEarlierFinding: This is the same inversion I identified at v29 as facet two of CLAUDE-V29-B1. It was resolved at v30 by making those indicators optional, and it returns here in mandatory, load-bearing form because fromBootLockdown is now the selected no-replacement policy rather than optional hardening.
shouldFix.theUnaddressedHalf: PTCB-V33-S1 asked for two things: define the load-option parse, and 'Bind the authenticated K entry to a required lockdown/kexec-enforcement capability or an independently attested policy.' The parse is defined in full and correctly. The capability binding is absent: I searched for capability, minimumVersion, minVersion, kexecEnforcement, enforcementCapability and declares, and nothing binds an enforcement capability to the authenticated kernel member. The only statement in that direction is prose in role — 'A machine that cannot honor sysctl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1 from OptionalData fails qualification' — whose sole enforcement is the same present-state read. Supplying the capability binding would also resolve the inversion, because a kernel member declaring that no kexec path exists could satisfy the policy without the sysctl needing to exist.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The failure is over-refusal. A machine that cannot kexec is turned away rather than wrongly attested, so no false assurance enters the negative-test matrix and the closure argument for machines that do qualify is unaffected. That places it with the determinacy and scope findings rather than the authenticity ones.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Treat an absent /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled as satisfying the policy when the authenticated kernel member is one on which no kexec path exists, rather than as a refusal — most directly by adding the capability binding PTCB-V33-S1 asked for, so the authenticated entry declares either kexec-absent or kexec-disabled-by-parameter and the present-state read corroborates the declared case. Then make requiredTokens conditional on that declaration so a kexec-less kernel is not required to carry a token for a sysctl it does not have, and propagate the conditional wording to both refusal enumerations.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V33-B1 — integrity lockdown still permitted a signed but undeclared executing kernel
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, and this is the substantive achievement of the generation. I want it on the record precisely because I have twice filed against this residual. fromBootLockdown now requires two tokens in the authenticated Boot#### OptionalData, lockdown=integrity and sysctl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1. The second is the one that matters: the kexec-disable toggle gates both the ordinary and the file-based kexec entry points, so setting it closes the signed path that integrity lockdown alone left open, and it cannot be cleared once set, so the property holds monotonically for the life of the launched kernel. Because the token sits inside the Boot#### VariableData that the signed transcript already authenticates as an EV_EFI_VARIABLE_BOOT row, the policy is established by firmware-measured evidence before userspace runs rather than by asking the running kernel about itself. That is Codex's second branch — 'attest and enforce a monotonic no-replacement policy that disables every kexec path before replacement can be staged and through observedAt' — and it is met. The reasoning is also non-circular in the direction that matters: if the launched kernel applies the parameter, no replacement can occur, so the kernel answering the corroborating reads is the launched kernel. NT-TCB-KEXEC is correspondingly restored as a fail-closed cell, and unlike v31 the mechanism now supports that description.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V33-S1 — fromBootLockdown did not define the load-option parse
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED for the parse half; see CLAUDE-V34-S2 for the capability half. loadOptionParse now gives the exact EFI_LOAD_OPTION layout — UINT32 Attributes little-endian, UINT16 FilePathListLength little-endian, CHAR16 Description including one terminating U+0000, then FilePathListLength bytes of device path, remainder OptionalData — with overrun, truncated Description, or a length past the end refusing. optionalDataEncoding pins the OptionalData as UTF-8 command line split on space, tab and newline with empty tokens discarded. tokenRules supplies the duplicate and override semantics Codex asked for: each required token exactly once, and a second lockdown= or sysctl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled= token refuses, which forecloses the later-wins override case. effectiveCmdline requires /proc/cmdline to contain both as whole tokens.

repairsVerified.finding: CLAUDE-V33-S1 (mine) — the mandatory condition appeared in none of the three scope and refusal enumerations
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED at all three, which is what I asked for. inScopeBootConfigs now states that an in-scope Boot#### OptionalData carries both tokens, that the present kernel selects integrity and that kexec_load_disabled is 1, and closes 'Signed and unsigned kexec are disabled by that measured policy.' refusesBootConfigs adds 'missing or duplicate fromBootLockdown tokens; malformed EFI_LOAD_OPTION; /proc/cmdline missing a required token; present lockdown not integrity; kexec_load_disabled not 1; kexec_loaded=1'. unavailableRefuses adds the corresponding conditions. limitsOfThisReview: I reviewed the claimed repairs against all three predecessor findings and the advisory, the new load-option parse and token policy, the closed change roster, the pin chain, the live register/COORD/file-04 carries and the authority refusals. Paths outside this round's roster were checked only for unchangedness, which is how the off-roster addition surfaced. My assessment that the kexec-disable toggle closes both entry points and cannot be cleared once set, and that the sysctl is absent on kernels built without kexec support, rests on the documented behaviour of the interfaces the clause names rather than on execution against a live machine; both findings I file would stand under any reading of those details, since the first is about roster accuracy and the second is resolved by the capability binding Codex already requested.
summary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX, and the rejection should not obscure what this generation achieved. The post-boot replacement residual that this row has carried since v28, and that I filed on at v28, v29 and v31, is now closed. fromBootLockdown requires sysctl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1 alongside lockdown=integrity inside the authenticated Boot#### OptionalData that the signed transcript already covers, and that toggle gates both kexec entry points and cannot be cleared once set, so the no-replacement property is established from firmware-measured evidence before userspace and holds monotonically. That meets Codex's second branch and earns the restoration of NT-TCB-KEXEC as a fail-closed cell, which v31 asserted without support and v34 supports. Codex's load-option parse finding is repaired in full, with field widths, endianness, the Description terminator, the OptionalData boundary and duplicate-token semantics all pinned, and my own v33 SHOULD-FIX is repaired at all three enumerations so the scope narrowing is visible where readers look. Two defects remain. First, the taxonomy disposition that repairs Codex's advisory was added at preKernelReferences/classForCodeRows, which no roster root names, while basedOn.method asserts that every unnamed path is unchanged from v33; the key does not exist in v33, so the assertion is false and the roster that bounds reviewer scope is inaccurate, though the change itself is correct. Second, the new mandatory kexecLoadDisabledNow refuses when the sysctl file is absent, which is exactly the state of a kernel built without kexec support, so the configuration on which replacement is structurally impossible is turned away while a fully replacement-capable kernel with the toggle set is admitted; this is the inversion I identified at v29, returning in mandatory form, and the capability binding Codex requested in the same finding — which would resolve it — was not added. Both are over-refusal and metadata-accuracy defects rather than authenticity holes, and both are cheap to close.
